items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was in the same band in Buffalo, NY, with Jimmy Crawford who played with Lunceford.

ctx.x: Why didn’t he want to leave?

I don’t know. I never delved into why he didn’t want to leave there. But he used to play with the same band that I played with around there when I was 14 or 15, playing with Earl Hood. His name escapes me right now but I always speak of him. He was one of the guys that was around there that never wanted to leave. And a saxophone player that I was telling you about that recommended me to Earl Hood, Paul Tyler. He was a great musician. He had been to New York. He was in the same band in Buffalo, NY, with Jimmy…
The band you were playing with there, Earl Hood, what sort of music would that band play? Was it written arrangements, was it mostly improvising?

items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: Lester gave Sweets Edison, called him Sweets because he played that sweet trumpet.

ctx.x: Well, I can't tell you that. You know, he was like Lester Young, who had a name for everybody. Lester gave Sweets Edison, called him Sweets because he played that sweet trumpet. He had a name for everybody, Lester.
But now, you -- what's Steel Chest now?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: They formed a band around there with Sy Oliver, Jimmy Crawford, Joe Thomas --

ctx.x: Were you sort of modeling it on Louie Armstrong?
Oh, definitely. Definitely. And then I played -- went to school until there was a band called Morrison's Grenadiers. They formed a band around there with Sy Oliver, Jimmy Crawford, Joe Thomas --
